sentences.1: A DPIA must describe the measures envisaged to address risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of personal data and demonstrate compliance with the Regulation.
sentences.10: A DPIA must address the rights of data subjects including information provision, right of access, right to rectification, and right to erasure.
sentences.2: the measures envisaged to address the risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of personal data and to demonstrate compliance with this Regulation taking into account the rights and legitimate interests of data subjects and other persons concerned
sentences.3: A DPIA does not require eradication of all risks but should help document risks and assess whether any remaining risks are justified.
sentences.4: But it should help you document them and assess whether or not any remaining risks are justified.
sentences.5: The Data Protection Impact Assessment and any ancillary documents;
sentences.6: If a DPO is present in the organization, the controller must seek the DPO's advice on the DPIA and document it as part of the process.
sentences.7: If you have a Data Protection Officer (DPO), you must ask for their advice on your DPIA, and document it as part of the process.
sentences.8: DPIAs are legally required for high-risk processing but can also bring broader compliance, financial and reputational benefits.
sentences.9: It's important to embed DPIAs into your organisational processes and ensure the outcome can influence your plans.
